# Rework round 6 claims (personal_loan_servicing)

PLS-R5-1: closed — the invented "two or more fee payment lines" restriction is gone from rule, policy baseline sentence and compute, together with every fee-payment and reversal read behind it. The records cannot link a fee payment reversal to the fee it unpaid, so the courtesy amount is now worked from quantities the records carry exactly: the waived fee's waivable part is its amount less every earlier waiver line applied to it, held to no more than the loan's fees balance (the late and returned-payment fees the loan still owes). The rule says outright that a fee payment on the fee, or a reversal of one, changes the waivable part only through the fees balance, and that the waiver comes off the fees the loan still owes, never refunding money. The overwrite's replaced_by (and its copy in the rule) now caps the amount at the loan's fees balance instead of the fee's still-unpaid part. Wherever the base grants a courtesy waiver for an unpaid part, the waivable part is at least that large, so no base-granted waiver is taken away. "Unpaid part" became "waivable part" throughout the policy's rule, ladders and quotes, and the waiver tool's docstring no longer calls the fee "unpaid".
XF#14 (task 0, one member; task 1, seven members): closed — every factor_sensitivity tier_taken in both task files was regenerated mechanically from the current ladders. The tier was decided by evaluating each factor on its task world, and every baseline_result was re-checked by substitution. The trace sentences were compared mechanically against the current factor ids, effects and cross labels. The retired-term sweep fixed the returned-fee "credited" trace (closed earlier, re-checked) and moved the courtesy amount, trace and dossier text to the waivable part.
R4-O1, R3-O1, R2-O3, R2-O4: carried — unchanged.
